Format proportions and percentages for presentation

Source: R/in_text_proportion.R
in_text_proportion.Rd

This is for formatting proportions, percentages and confidence intervals for reporting. Confidence intervals are calculated usingbinom::binom.confint. Formatting is performed using table1::round_pad.

Usage

in_text_proportion(
  x,
  n,
  output = c("proportion", "percentage")[1],
  output_format = c("p", "xn", "xp", "xnp")[4],
  digits_proportion = 3,
  digits_percent = 1,
  ci_method = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a numeric vector for the numerator.

n

a numeric vector for the denominator. If length(x) > 1 and length(n) == 1, the denominator is assumed to be the same for all values of x.

output

a string specifying the type of output requested: either "percentage" or "proportion". Defaults to proportion.

output_format

a string specifying the formatting of the output, which may include the numerator, the denominator, and percentage/proportion: one of "p" (proportion only), "xn" (numerator and denominator), "xp" (numerator and proportion/percentage), or "xnp" (numerator/denominator and proportion/percentage)

digits_proportion

the digits of precision for proportions (see table1::round_pad).

digits_percent

the digits of precision for percentages (see table1::round_pad).

ci_method

a string containing the type of interval estimate to compute, if any. See ?binom::binom.confint.

level

the confidence/credible interval coefficient

...

other arguments passed to binom::binom.confint

Value

When a CI is computed, the result is a list, containing the output and individual components: otherwise, the result is a string.

Examples

# Calculating percentages
in_text_proportion(x = 2, n = 10, output_format = "p")
#> [1] "0.2"
in_text_proportion(x = 0, n = 10, output_format = "xp")
#> [1] "0 (0)"
in_text_proportion(x = 10, n = 10, output_format = "xnp")
#> [1] "10/10 (1)"

in_text_proportion(x = 2, n = 10, output = "proportion", output_format = "p")
#> [1] "0.2"
in_text_proportion(x = 0, n = 10, output = "proportion", output_format = "xp")
#> [1] "0 (0)"
in_text_proportion(x = 10, n = 10, output = "proportion", output_format = "xnp")
#> [1] "10/10 (1)"

in_text_proportion(x = 1, n = 1e4, output_format = "xp", digits_percent = 2)
#> [1] "1 (0.00)"
in_text_proportion(x = 1, n = 1e4, output_format = "xp", digits_percent = 2)
#> [1] "1 (0.00)"

in_text_proportion(x = 0, n = 10, output_format = "p", ci_method = "bayes")
#> $x
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $n
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $output
#> [1] "0"
#> 
#> $output_ci
#> [1] " (95% CI: 0.000, 0.171)"
#> 
#> $ci
#>   method x  n       mean lower     upper
#> 1  bayes 0 10 0.04545455     0 0.1707731
#> 
#> $lcl_rounded
#> [1] "0.000"
#> 
#> $ucl_rounded
#> [1] "0.171"
#> 
#> $ci_string
#> [1] "(95% CI: 0.000, 0.171)"
#> 
#> $level
#> [1] 0.95
#> 
in_text_proportion(x = 0, n = 10, output_format = "p", ci_method = "exact")
#> $x
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $n
#> [1] 10
#> 
#> $output
#> [1] "0"
#> 
#> $output_ci
#> [1] " (95% CI: 0.000, 0.308)"
#> 
#> $ci
#>   method x  n mean lower     upper
#> 1  exact 0 10    0     0 0.3084971
#> 
#> $lcl_rounded
#> [1] "0.000"
#> 
#> $ucl_rounded
#> [1] "0.308"
#> 
#> $ci_string
#> [1] "(95% CI: 0.000, 0.308)"
#> 
#> $level
#> [1] 0.95
#>
